title: qa(checklist): correct five assertion defects from the 18.4.0 acceptance
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao7ZAVswsAUT1r3cMHd6LWKg)_

Fixes #32945

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：平台测试清单里五个条目的验收断言改正（权限集账本、MCP read_file 预算、os deploy 确认、命名空间共有者残余项、命名空间与对象重名的发布门），各升一个 revision 并补 history。
- 为什么改：18.4.0 验收跑（#32940）发现这五处是清单写错了 fixture 或断言，产品行为是对的；不改每次发版验收都会误报红。
- 风险与回滚：只改清单 JSON 文本，不动产品代码、不发布任何包；回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json`（条款 2 语义反转最大），`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json`（含一个待你裁决的问题），`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm check:platform-checklist`，预期 `OK — 16 areas, 427 items`，锚点全部解析。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（read_file 预算停在零页时是否必须带 `truncated: true` 的问题见下方 Acceptance notes，裁决可后补）。

## What changes

Checklist text only. No product code, no pins, no changeset (`skip-changeset`: nothing under any package's `files[]` moves). Each item gets a revision bump and a `history` row with `ref: #32945`.

1. **`access-security.permission-set-address-in-execution-context` r2 → r3, acceptance[1].** Step 2's row names `com.qa.addr-b`, which holds no `qa_a_reader`. That makes it a stale column, not a second holder. The ledger reads a stale column by the D3 rule with no caller and switches off the holder that rule answers (`com.qa.addr-a`), so M loses the set. The clause now asserts that live (M loses the set; explain says `held — deactivated`; deleting the row restores it). The real two-holder case cannot be reached through install (the item's knownGaps), so it is scored from the pin. steps[1], negative[0] and the evidence line change with it.
2. **`ai.mcp-read-file-pdf-word-extraction` r1 → r2, acceptance[3].** At `OS_MCP_READ_FILE_CPU_BUDGET_MS=1` the budget runs out before page one, so `pdfAnswer`'s empty arm answers `content: 'none'` with the budget sentence as the note and no `truncated`. The fixture budget becomes 60 ms. The step says to raise or lower the budget until some pages are read, and to record the value. The clause names the zero-page shape as a fixture signal, not a verdict. Also, the `receipt` field is on `showcase_invoice_line`, so the fixture and steps now name the invoice line.
3. **`cli.deploy-runtime-dry-run-json` r1 → r2, acceptance[3].** v1.1.0 used to drop `note`. A removed field keeps its column, so nothing asks for confirmation and `--json` installs. v1.1.0 now renames `note` → `memo` with no `renamedFrom`. That is a suspected rename, which the runtime stops with 409 `SCHEMA_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and the confirm command. A negative now marks a drop-only fixture as a fixture error.
4. **`platform-core.namespace-co-owner-name-refusal` r3 → r4, acceptance[2].** `os validate` on a `packages[]` stack with a residual `qa_board` exits 0 by design, because the CLI does not judge the residual. The manifest service does. The clause records the exit 0 and scores the judgement from `manifest-service-residual-namespace-name.test.ts`. The oracle stays `build`, and the evidence adds the pin's summary line. The ref list gains that pin.
5. **`platform-core.namespace-object-name-refusal` r1 → r2, acceptance[2] (and clause 1's fixture).** `POST /packages/:id/publish` publishes the package items the metadata service holds, not drafts. On this fixture it answers 200 `success: false` "No metadata items found for package". The drafts door is `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts`. It answers 200 with `outcome: 'refused'` and `failed[0].code: 'NAMESPACE_CONFLICT'`, and keeps the draft. The step and clause now name that route and answer, and spell out the per-item publish route (`POST /meta/object/NAME/publish?package=…`). Clause 1 now validates a stack whose `packages[]` composes both packages, because the clashing directory alone validates 0.

## Verification

Each new shape was read against `main` @ `cf1b55c0`:

- **Stale ledger column.** `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` `ledgerRowHolders`, doc: "a null one — or a stale one, whose package no longer serves the name — is read by the D3 rule with no caller, and keeps disabling the holder that rule answers"; and the `not-held-by-qualifier` arm: "A stale column the catalog refuses because the holder the rule answers is outside its package's namespace ... still switches that holder off: a switch-off is never read as none." Two-holder pin: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-set-address.test.ts` "a holder of a grant the user does not hold switches nothing off for the one they do".
- **Zero-page budget answer.** `packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts` `pdfAnswer`: `if (!joined) { return { kind: 'none', reason: budgetNote ?? '...no text layer...' } }`; the text arm sets `truncated: truncated || parts.length < numPages || budgetNote !== undefined`. `renderReadFile` sets `facts.truncated` only for `kind === 'text'` and sets `facts.content = 'none'; facts.note = extracted.reason` otherwise. `cpuBudgetNote`: "Reading stopped at the CPU-time budget for one file (${budgetMs} ms) after ${read}...".
- **receipt field.** `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts`: `receipt: Field.file({ label: 'Receipt' })` sits on `InvoiceLine` (`name: 'showcase_invoice_line'`).
- **Upgrade verdict.** `packages/metadata-core/src/package-upgrade-verdict.ts` `schemaUpgradeVerdict`: "A suspected rename always needs confirming ... Removed fields, removed objects, `safe` type changes and seed changes are reported by a dry run and refused by nothing." `package-upgrade-plan.ts` records a suspected rename when a stored field is removed and a stored one added on the same object. `packages/cli/src/commands/deploy.ts` prints `Deploying this build would stop for your confirmation — ${wouldStop.length} finding(s):` and `confirm: os deploy --confirm-upgrade ${findingSet}`. `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` answers `409 SCHEMA_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`.
- **Residual not judged by the CLI.** `packages/objectql/src/namespace-co-owner-names.ts`: "`os validate` / `os build` do not judge the residual, and need not ..."; `packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts`: "the residual ... is not judged at either door". Pin: `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-namespace-name.test.ts` "is refused at the manifest service, naming both holders, and the artifact is put back whole".
- **Drafts door.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`: `/publish` judges `packageObjectNames(metadataService, id)` then `publishPackage`; `/publish-drafts` routes through `protocol.publishPackageDrafts`. `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`: "No metadata items found for package '${packageId}'". Pin: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.namespace-object-name-doors.test.ts` expects `{ success: false, outcome: 'refused', publishedCount: 0, failedCount: 1 }`, `failed[0].code: 'NAMESPACE_CONFLICT'`, the draft still a draft. Per-item route: `packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts` `POST {metaPath}/:type/:name/publish`, `req.query.package`.
- **Live evidence.** QA run #32940 (F-4 to F-8 and its R4/R5 comments), quoted in the card.

## Acceptance notes

- **Open question for the maintainer (item 2).** When the CPU budget runs out before any PDF page is read, `read_file` answers `content: 'none'` with the budget sentence and no `truncated`. If a stopped read must always carry `truncated: true`, that is a product defect in `pdfAnswer`'s empty arm (`packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts`), not a checklist fix. This PR does not decide it. The clause treats the zero-page shape as no FAIL until it is ruled, and the seat raises the question.
- No live run was made for the corrected clauses. They are scored from source at `cf1b55c0` and from the #32940 run bodies. The 60 ms budget is a host-dependent starting point; the step says to adjust it and record the value.
- The two pins named as scoring sources (`permission-set-address.test.ts`, `manifest-service-residual-namespace-name.test.ts`) were not run locally: this diff changes no code they test. CI's `Test Core` runs them.
